text.arabic_uthmani: ذَٰلِكَ جَزَيْنَٰهُم بِمَا كَفَرُوا۟ ۖ وَهَلْ نُجَٰزِىٓ إِلَّا ٱلْكَفُورَ

words.gloss_range: distal demonstrative pointing back to the prior punitive outcome as an identifiable whole

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: completed divine requital verb that classifies the fronted outcome

words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}) opens by pointing back to the visible outcome of the previous ayah and compressing the flood, replacement, and scarcity into one object. Because the demonstrative is fronted before {{ar:جَزَيْنَٰهُم}} ({{tr:jazaynāhum}}), the reader faces the already displayed result first, then hears it classified as measured requital rather than loose disaster.

topics.headline: prior outcome compressed into one object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word gathers the prior flood, replacement, and scarcity into a single evidence-object for judgment.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence identifies the demonstrative as a fronted object pointing back to the preceding punitive replacement event, so the CRITICAL compression claim is locally licensed.

topics.headline: fronted evidence before agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that visible ruin is presented before the verb of requital, making the clause feel like adjudication of evidence already on display.
topics.reason: The demonstrative is syntactically the fronted explicit object of the following requital verb, and the boundary rows correctly read this as a shift from seeing the ruin to interpreting it.

words.gloss_range: completed divine requital of the addressed group; locally punitive because the stated cause is their covering or ingratitude
words.root_gloss_range: recompense, requital, repayment, reward, penalty, settlement, sufficing, and debt-collection branches; the local verb selects measured recompense rather than tribute or fiscal-payment branches

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: causal phrase that narrows recompense to adverse requital
later Form III imperfect reprise of the recompense root

words.prose: {{ar:جَزَيْنَٰهُم}} ({{tr:jazaynāhum}}) makes the prior outcome a completed divine settlement: the subject marker and object suffix keep agency and the punished group in one compact verb. The {{ar:ج ز ي}} ({{tr:j-z-y}}) root can cover reward or penalty, but the following cause in {{ar:بِمَا كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:bimā kafarū}}) narrows it here to adverse requital, a matched and sufficient return answering what they did. As a Form I perfect, this first occurrence prepares the later Form III {{ar:نُجَٰزِىٓ}} ({{tr:nujāzī}}), so the finished case becomes the evidence for a standing rule.

topics.headline: completed divine act with the group as object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the disaster is not merely something that happened to the group; the verb assigns them as recipients of a completed divine requital.
topics.reason: The perfect first-person plural verb with attached third-person plural object pronoun directly supports completed agency and recipienthood.

topics.headline: neutral recompense root narrowed to adverse settlement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the account-settlement force of the root while also seeing why the local cause makes the settlement punitive.
topics.reason: V4 supports a broad recompense and sufficing range, but local grammar attaches the cause through the following prepositional phrase, so reward, tribute, and unrelated sufficiency branches are not selected as local senses.

topics.headline: first root occurrence prepares the final rule
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first requital verb is not isolated narrative; it sets up the later return of the same root as a generalizing principle.
topics.reason: The ayah contains two locally aligned {{ar:ج ز ي}} ({{tr:j-z-y}}) verbs with different aspect and form, supporting the event-to-rule movement claimed by the CRITICAL rows.

words.gloss_range: prefixed preposition locally functioning as causal/basis marker for the following clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: following causal content governed by the prefixed preposition

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) is the small hinge that binds requital to cause. It attaches to {{ar:مَا كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:mā kafarū}}), so the prior devastation is not left as arbitrary loss; what they covered, denied, or failed to acknowledge becomes both the reason for requital and the measure by which it is assessed.

topics.headline: causal hinge inside the compact phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition turns the report into explanation by tying divine requital directly to the human cause.
topics.reason: The preposition has multiple possible values in general, but the local attachment to the causal complement after a requital verb licenses causal and basis force rather than accompaniment or instrument.

words.gloss_range: relative or masdariyyah particle governed by the prefixed preposition, keeping both object-focused and act-focused blame available

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: prefixed preposition governing the causal particle
interrogative particle beginning the later restrictive question
exception particle that narrows the final recipient class

words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) keeps the ground of requital deliberately open. Governed by {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}), it can point to what they denied and to their denying as an act, so the cause remains broad while the later {{ar:هَلْ}} ({{tr:hal}}) ... {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) construction narrows the recipient class.

topics.headline: open causal scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cause is not forced into one narrow object; the phrase can hold both the act of denial and what was denied.
topics.reason: The input grammar explicitly allows relative or masdariyyah analysis, and the following verb can stand intransitively or with an elided object, so the broad causal reading is licensed.

topics.headline: broad offense before narrow class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the contrast between an expansive causal phrase and the final restricted class that alone receives this requital.
topics.reason: The first clause leaves the offense semantically broad, while the final rhetorical restriction limits the object to the intensive ingrate type.

words.gloss_range: completed collective covering, denial, or ingratitude functioning as the cause of requital
words.root_gloss_range: covering and concealment, denial or rejection of truth, covering over favor as ingratitude, disavowal, and other remote concrete branches; locally the moral covering/denial/ingratitude branches are active

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: final intensive adjective that turns the plural act into a restricted character type

words.prose: {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}) names the cause as a completed collective act. Its {{ar:ك ف ر}} ({{tr:k-f-r}}) range keeps covering, denial, and ingratitude together: they covered over what should have remained acknowledged. The base form leaves that charge broad, while the variant that names divine favor and the later {{ar:ٱلْكَفُورَ}} ({{tr:al-kafūra}}) show that ingratitude is a central pressure, not a marginal gloss.

topics.headline: settled plural act as cause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the recompense answers a settled communal act, not a passing lapse or unnamed misfortune.
topics.reason: The perfect third-person plural verb supplies the compact subject and completes the causal subordinate clause.

topics.headline: covering image becomes moral ingratitude
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the charge is wider than a flat disbelief label: it is a covering-over of favor or truth that makes requital intelligible.
topics.reason: V4 supports covering, denial, and ingratitude branches; the local setting after Saba's favor licenses moral covering and ingratitude, while remote branches such as darkness, farmer, place-name, camphor, and expiation are not local senses.

topics.headline: plural act moves toward final type
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the root returns from the causal verb to the final intensive type, turning historical behavior into a criterion for judgment.
topics.reason: The same {{ar:ك ف ر}} ({{tr:k-f-r}}) root appears in the causal verb and the final intensive adjective, and the attachment data places the latter as the restricted object of requital.

words.gloss_range: conjunction linking the completed report to a restrictive rhetorical question
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the report-to-rule pivot. It keeps the final question connected to the completed explanation while also marking a new speech act: the ayah moves from narrated recompense into a restrictive principle about who fits such requital.

topics.headline: connected pivot into the question
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing question is an interpretive extension of the case, not a detached aphorism.
topics.reason: The conjunction begins the contrast-linked final verbal clause and directly precedes the interrogative particle, matching the CRITICAL claim of a connected pivot.

words.gloss_range: interrogative particle whose local force becomes rhetorical restrictive negation with the following exception particle

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: exception particle that gives the question restrictive force

words.prose: {{ar:هَلْ}} ({{tr:hal}}) keeps the clause in question form while the following {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) gives it restrictive force. The reader is made to test the possible recipients and arrive at the implied exclusion: none but the final named type fits this requital. That question-shaped tail turns Saba's case into a rule by challenge rather than by flat statement.

topics.headline: question form with restrictive force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah states exclusivity by making the listener enact the exclusion through a question.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence explicitly flags the {{ar:هَلْ}} ({{tr:hal}}) ... {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) construction as restrictive rhetorical force, not a neutral information request.

topics.headline: specific case turned into rule
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final question does not add a new event; it converts the narrated case into a general accountability principle.
topics.reason: The final clause follows the completed report and is syntactically marked as a restrictive rhetorical question, so its tail-function is locally supported.

words.gloss_range: active first-person plural imperfect Form III requital, locally a standing rule of responsive dealing bounded by the final object
words.root_gloss_range: recompense, requital, reciprocal return, settlement, sufficing, debt-collection, tribute, and prevailing-in-requital branches; locally the active Form III recompense branch is selected

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: root family that characterizes the recipient by denial and ingratitude
passive Form III variant used as contrast for the standard active verb
passive base-form variant used as contrast for the standard active verb
exception particle that confines the object of requital
final intensive adjective serving as the restricted object

words.prose: {{ar:نُجَٰزِىٓ}} ({{tr:nujāzī}}) returns the {{ar:ج ز ي}} ({{tr:j-z-y}}) root in a different mode: active, first-person, imperfect, and Form III. The standard form keeps divine agency audible while the imperfect makes the finished Saba case into a standing practice of responsive dealing-back with the agent characterized by {{ar:ك ف ر}} ({{tr:k-f-r}}). Passive variants such as {{ar:يُجَازَى}} ({{tr:yujāzā}}) and {{ar:يُجْزَى}} ({{tr:yujzā}}) show that the clause could be cast as a maxim, but the standard wording keeps the speaker visible while {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) confines the object to {{ar:ٱلْكَفُورَ}} ({{tr:al-kafūra}}).

topics.headline: active imperfect divine agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the general rule remains spoken with explicit divine agency rather than becoming anonymous policy.
topics.reason: The standard verb is active first-person plural imperfect, and the attachment data identifies the implicit subject as divine narration.

topics.headline: passive variants as contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the passive variants illuminate a possible maxim-like casting, while the standard reading keeps active divine speech in force.
topics.reason: Accepted variant readings are valid contrastive evidence, but they do not override the canonical local parse as active with the final noun as object.

topics.headline: responsive requital bounded by final type
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb does not describe indiscriminate punishment; it frames calibrated dealing-back and is bounded to the intensive ingrate type.
topics.reason: The Form III verb directly governs the final intensive adjective under the exception construction, supporting reciprocal response and restricted object scope.

topics.headline: same root shifts from event to law
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same recompense root carries the ayah from completed history into a standing legal-moral principle.
topics.reason: The local repetition of {{ar:ج ز ي}} ({{tr:j-z-y}}) with aspect and form shift supports the CRITICAL claim that recurrence marks a move from finished case to rule.

words.gloss_range: exceptive/restrictive particle producing exclusive scope after the rhetorical interrogative

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: interrogative particle whose question form works with exception
final definite intensive class label restricted by the exception
recited restrictive unit joining exception and class label

words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) supplies the hard restriction in the closing question. After {{ar:هَلْ}} ({{tr:hal}}), it excludes other recipients and leaves the final noun as the only class under the verb. Its position right before {{ar:ٱلْكَفُورَ}} ({{tr:al-kafūra}}) delays the verdict class until the ayah's last word, and the recited unit {{ar:إِلَّا ٱلْكَفُورَ}} ({{tr:illā al-kafūra}}) lets the exception press directly into the class label.

topics.headline: exception becomes exclusive scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle controls the whole closing clause by excluding every class except the final one.
topics.reason: The guardrail evidence marks the construction as restrictive rhetorical force and identifies the final noun as object under the restriction.

topics.headline: boundary before the final class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict class is held back until closure, so the exception particle and final noun land as one restrictive unit.
topics.reason: The particle is separate and immediately precedes the final definite adjective, so the CRITICAL boundary and delay claims are locally grounded.

words.gloss_range: definite singular intensive adjective naming the restricted object as an ingrained ingrate type
words.root_gloss_range: covering and concealment, denial or rejection of truth, ingratitude for favor, disavowal, expiation, farmer, darkness, place-name, camphor, and other remote branches; locally the intensive moral ingratitude and denial branches are selected

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: active requital verb that governs the final adjective as object
nominative passive-variant form that foregrounds the same final type
earlier plural verb naming the act that becomes the final type

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْكَفُورَ}} ({{tr:al-kafūra}}) is the ayah's final landing word. It is a definite singular intensive adjective functioning as the object of {{ar:نُجَٰزِىٓ}} ({{tr:nujāzī}}), so the closing rule is not aimed at everyone but at the ingrained ingrate type. Passive variants can raise {{ar:ٱلْكَفُورُ}} ({{tr:al-kafūru}}) as subject, but the standard accusative keeps {{ar:ٱلْكَفُورَ}} ({{tr:al-kafūra}}) as the object of active divine requital while preserving the same restricted class. The root's covering image remains morally active: the plural act {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}) becomes a settled character label, and morphology, restriction, and final position make that type carry the verdict.

topics.headline: definite singular intensive archetype
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word names an ingrained moral type rather than merely repeating the plural actors of the story.
topics.reason: The local form is definite, singular, and intensive, and attachment evidence identifies it as the object of the active requital verb under the restriction.

topics.headline: case contrast preserves the same restricted class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that passive variants can foreground the final type as subject, while the standard reading keeps it as the object of active divine requital.
topics.reason: The variant case shift is valid contrastive evidence, but the standard accusative object parse governs the local prose.

topics.headline: covering image intensified into character
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that extreme ingratitude is pictured as repeated concealment of what should remain visible, not as a colorless label.
topics.reason: The physical covering branch can illuminate the moral branch, but local grammar and context select intensive moral ingratitude and denial, not remote concrete branches.

topics.headline: restriction and closure converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that morphology, restriction, and final position converge so the named type becomes the sole class fitted to the verdict.
topics.reason: The final noun is the restricted object after the exception particle and occupies ayah-final position, supporting the CRITICAL closure and class-boundary claims.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The doubled ج ز ي at words 2 and 6 around causal بما, together with the move from كفروا to the intensive الكفور.
baseline_models.mechanism: The matching-act branch of ج ز ي makes a closed return circuit: an act of covering or denial generates a corresponding outcome, while repeated ك ف ر moves from deed to settled disposition. The restrictive question marks the return as principled rather than arbitrary.

activation_trace.role: Matching an act with its consequence supplies the reciprocal engine for both focus verbs.
Blocking truth supplies both the causal deed and the intensive agent's settled orientation.

changed_reading.after: The verse states an act-shaped return: repeated covering hardens into the disposition for which the corresponding ruinous return is reserved.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The causal بما كفروا and intensive الكفور, read through the debt branch of ج ز ي and the concealed-blessing branch of ك ف ر.
baseline_models.mechanism: Covering a blessing withholds the acknowledgment due for it; the debt-collection branch of ج ز ي then construes the consequence as settlement of an outstanding relational liability rather than an unrelated penalty.

activation_trace.role: Demanding and collecting a debt supplies the settlement mechanism for recompense.
Concealing a blessing supplies the unpaid acknowledgment that makes the relation liable.

changed_reading.after: Persistent nonacknowledgment turns a received blessing into an unsettled account whose consequence is collection.

context_deltas.mechanism: Elsewhere the same root names favorable recompense, including doubled return, while 34:33 repeats a هل ... إلا restriction and ties recompense to performed deeds. The focus question therefore restricts this ruinous mode of recompense to the deeply ungrateful; it does not make ج ز ي itself exclusively punitive.

activation_trace.role: Matching action and consequence supplies the focus rule whose scope is being qualified.
The same matching branch names favorable return to believing and sound action, showing that recompense is not lexically punitive.
A second restrictive recompense question makes the returned outcome answer to what was done.
Intentional action supplies the measure to which the negative return corresponds.
Named favorable recompense confirms that the root spans both directions of return.
Increase by another like amount shows that favorable correspondence can exceed bare numerical equivalence.

structural_cues: 34:4 applies ج ز ي to believers, while 34:37 names a doubled جزاء.
34:33 repeats هل ... إلا with recompense explicitly bounded by what was done.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies favorable and unfavorable ج ز ي uses plus a second restrictive question; I infer that 34:17 ellipses 'this ruinous kind of recompense,' not recompense absolutely. A live alternative is class-limited rhetoric without a semantic ellipsis.

changed_reading.before: The question can sound as though only the kafur ever receives recompense.
changed_reading.after: Recompense is bilateral and can be generous; only this destructive, deed-matched mode is reserved for the entrenched ingrate.

context_deltas.mechanism: The local sequence defines prosperity as apportioned provision whose expected output is gratitude, then keeps the slot of two gardens while substituting their yield after the people turn away. Focus branches make ج ز ي a counter-substitution: provision is answered in the same material channel by replacement produce, settling the gratitude they covered.

activation_trace.role: One thing standing in another's place casts the consequence as a counter-value replacing the prior benefit.
Concealing blessing identifies the missing relational response as gratitude, not merely abstract assent.
Recognition of blessing and praise of its giver establish the positive response expected from received abundance.
An apportioned gift identifies the gardens' produce as received provision rather than self-grounded possession.
Turning one's side away supplies the deliberate break between provision and acknowledgment.
One thing replacing another gives the consequence its explicit substitution mechanism.
Tree and crop yield locates the substitution in the productive output of the same garden frame.

structural_cues: 34:13 says few servants are شكور, and 34:15 imperatively joins eating provision to gratitude.
34:16 repeats جنتين across the exchange but changes the yield immediately before 34:17's deictic ذلك and causal بما.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies provision, commanded gratitude, deliberate turning, and substituted yield; I infer that the material replacement is the functional form taken by ج ز ي. A live alternative is that the flood and poor produce are generic punishment rather than a deliberately same-channel counter-gift.

changed_reading.before: The lost gardens are simply a penalty for disbelief.
changed_reading.after: The altered gardens are a material counter-gift: covered provision is settled by provision's substitution with a diminished, hostile yield.

context_deltas.mechanism: Measured, connected travel in 34:18 is followed by a request to create distance and then by tearing and dispersal in 34:19. The focus return rule is reenacted: desired spacing is granted in destructive excess, converting traversable intervals into rupture and the people into scattered report.

activation_trace.role: Matching action with consequence supplies the rule that the following travel sequence reenacts.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the ordered shift from measured connection to requested distance to fragmentation; I supply the arrow that the request semantically scripts the form of return. context_deltas.mechanism: The closing sequence orders panic, failed escape, an impossible attempt to reach faith from afar, prior kufr, and finally a barrier from desire. This temporal-spatial closure activates the focus shift from the finite كفروا to intensive الكفور: the ruinous return tracks persistent covering until access itself is lost.

activation_trace.role: Repeated blocking of truth supplies the disposition whose persistence is tested by the closing sequence.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the temporal-spatial sequence and the repeated focus root; I infer that intensive الكفور names persistence whose terminal recompense is lost access. A live alternative is that the intensive form marks degree only, without encoding duration.

changed_reading.after: الكفور marks a covering disposition sustained until the possibility of reversal is spatially and temporally cut off.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's split ج ز ز mapping for focus ج ز ي and the agricultural branch of ك ف ر. It remains valid as an activation because both are explicit focus inventories and the local context is gardens and yield. Render only as a controlled harvest image, not as a claim that جَزَى lexically means cutting here.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, repeated covering is a sowing that ripens to its own cutting, with the changed garden yield as the crop gathered.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it links distinct roots by shared covering images and the local غفور/كفور intensive-form echo, not by etymology. surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The intensive الكفور at focus word 8, with ك ف ر branches of covering generally and covering blessing specifically.

activation_trace.role: General covering supplies the human act that can be set against a different protective covering.
Covering blessing specifies that the human concealment suppresses the gift relation.
Covering a fault while protecting its bearer supplies the nearby divine counter-image.
Acknowledging blessing identifies the response that should mediate between protective covering and received gift.

changed_reading.after: As a contained echo, the kafur perversely answers the nearby forgiving protective cover with an inverse cover that hides the blessing itself.

strongest_changes: The second question restricts ruinous recompense, not ج ز ي as a whole; the surah also uses the root for favorable and doubled return.
Kufr becomes concrete ingratitude toward apportioned provision, and jaza becomes material counter-substitution in the gardens' yield.
Demanded distance returns as fragmentation, while persistent covering ends in failed reach and a barrier from desire.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context exposed a repeated return mechanism: blessing calls for acknowledgment, refusal is answered in the same material or spatial channel, and persistence converts reversible distance into terminal separation.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether 34:18-19 is best read as a second enactment of 34:17's rule or only as subsequent narrative consequence.
The exact scope of the ellipsis after نُجَازِى remains inferential.
The harvest and rival-coverings activations depend on split-root or echo mechanisms and should remain exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Recompense mirrors the covering of favor.** `ج ز ي/B001` is recompense matching an act and `ك ف ر/B004` covering over a favor. The root of recompense encloses two forms while ingratitude names what triggered it. Covering is the input and matched return the rule; the lost productive cover of the gardens becomes the material analogue. The packet supplies the matching language and prior landscape; I infer that ecological degradation makes concealed favor visible by withdrawing its function. The ayah reads recompense as disclosure through a matched reversal, not arbitrary penalty.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 34:37’s doubled recompense preserved the matching principle while changing its output from degraded yield to secure elevation.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **An isomorphic return for covered favor.** `ك ف ر B004` supplies covering over a favor, and `ج ز ي B001` supplies recompense matching an act. Gratitude frames the productive works of 34:13 and the gardens of 34:15; 34:16 then replaces the covering gardens after the favor is covered over in refusal. The branches assign concealment to the offense and matched substitution to the response. The packet supplies both sides; I infer that the material loss mirrors the perceptual act. Recompense reads as an enacted likeness between ingratitude and the withdrawal of beneficent cover.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 34:20-21 corrected any deterministic reading of this recompense. The expectation is fulfilled through following, yet the tempter has no coercive authority; the matching consequence remains anchored in enacted refusal.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Çekirdek yalnızca bağışlama değildir; günah veya bozulmuş yemin karşısında yükü gideren bir işlem ya da karşılık bulunur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Günah yükünü giderme çekirdeği korunur; bozulmuş yemin için gerekeni yapma yalnızca ilgili söz öbeğine bağlı özel gerçekleşmedir.

concept_map.definition: Bir günahın ya da bozulan yeminin doğurduğu yükü, gereken karşılığı veya işlemi yerine getirerek örtmek, silmek ve işlenmemiş sayılacak duruma getirmektir.

facets.statement: Günahın yükünü örten veya silen karşılık ya da işlem.
Bozulan yemin için gereken yükümlülüğü yerine getirme, çekirdeğin yapıya bağlı özel türüdür.
İşlemin sonucu, kötülüğün işlenmemiş gibi değerlendirilmesi veya etkisinin silinmesidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar günahın veya yeminin yükünü gideren karşılıkta birleşir; toplu anlatım hem gereken eylemi hem de günahın silinmiş sayılması sonucunu korur.
